sections.h2: Where does a Scott County, Kentucky tax bill come from?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The PVA fixes what a Scott County parcel is worth. The sheriff mails the bill and takes payment, and its own page insists the office never sets a value. It collects for 28 districts, among them the state, the county, school systems, fire and library districts and, by contract, some cities. Mailing normally happens on November 1. For a value you dispute, call the PVA at (502) 863-7885. For payment questions, call the sheriff at (502) 863-7855.

Georgetown adds its own levy. City hall's Clerk's Office takes payment over the counter, by post or by phone, and lookup and online payment run through the city's OpenGov portal. Bills from before 2025 are found through the city's Tax Master service. A house inside Georgetown carries a city bill in addition to the county one.

sections.h2: How is Scott County laid out, and what shaped it?
sections.html:
Scott County lies north of Lexington in the Bluegrass and is counted in the Lexington-Fayette metro. Lawmakers split it from Woodford County in 1792 and honored Gen. Charles Scott. Its 285 square miles include only 3.7 of water, and seven counties touch it: Grant, Harrison, Bourbon, Fayette, Woodford, Franklin and Owen. Georgetown holds both the courthouse and the largest population, while Sadieville and Stamping Ground are the two smaller cities.

The county grew quickly: 33,061 residents in 2000, 47,173 in 2010 and 57,155 in 2020. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 62,262, an increase of 8.9 percent since 2020.

  • Georgetown began as Lebanon, the name Elijah Craig gave his 1782 settlement, and was renamed for George Washington in 1790.
  • Elijah Craig, who led that settlement, is credited with early mills and possibly the area's first bourbon.
  • The Choctaw Nation operated the Choctaw Academy at Blue Spring in the county from 1825 until 1842.
  • Voters approved countywide alcohol sales in 2019.

Interstate 75 runs along the east side of Georgetown, with exits 125, 126, 127 and 129, and Lexington is about 16 miles south. US 25, 62 and 460 also serve the city. Georgetown College sits downtown.

sections.h2: How much does Toyota shape the Scott County market?
sections.html:
Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky opened in Georgetown in 1988, its first wholly owned plant in the United States, and it builds the Camry, Lexus ES and RAV4. The city's 2018 annual financial report listed it as the top employer with 10,019 workers, well ahead of Scott County Schools at 1,219. The Census Bureau counts 26,711 jobs at county employers in 2023.

Schools shape demand too. Scott County Schools runs nine elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, and Great Crossing High School opened in 2019 as population climbed. Know which school zone your house falls in before you list it, because relocating families ask.

sections.h2: How does Scott County housing compare statewide?
sections.html:
Prices here sit well above the Kentucky norm. QuickFacts shows a typical owner-occupied home at $288,500 and a typical household income of $85,158 for 2020 to 2024. Builders took out 393 permits in 2025, so a resale competes with new construction.

  • Households: 22,642, with an estimated 25,010 housing units by July 1, 2025.
  • Homeowners hold 71.7 percent of occupied units, and rent in the middle is $1,247.
  • Owner costs with a mortgage run $1,637 a month, against $514 without one.
  • Commutes average 22.2 minutes, and 34.7 percent of adults finished a four-year degree.
  • Poverty touches 8.8 percent of residents.

In 2020 the median resident was 36.2 years old, about two in three residents lived in urban areas and just 6.2 percent of housing units stood vacant.

sections.h2: Which Georgetown landmarks and conditions affect a sale?
sections.html:
Georgetown became a railroad hub after the Civil War, tied to Cincinnati, Louisville and Frankfort lines, and Confederate raiders under John Hunt Morgan struck the town on July 15, 1862 and July 10, 1864. Its downtown business section is the Oxford Historic District, which is on the National Register of Historic Places. Ward Hall, a Greek Revival mansion just outside town, is listed there too.

Near the old downtown, call the city before you plan any exterior work to prepare for a sale. Georgetown's humid subtropical climate delivers about 45 inches of rain a year, with the wettest months in late spring and summer, so roof and drainage condition draw the closest looks from buyers.

sections.h2: Which dates and charges govern a Scott County bill?
sections.html:
The calendar comes from KRS 134.015. A 2 percent discount rewards full payment by November 1, the face amount applies through December 31, January adds 5 percent, and later payment costs 10 percent.

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax personally, and a delinquent bill leaves a lien on the land itself. Spell out the split in your sales contract so the closing agent knows what to deduct from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What happens when a Scott County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Around April 15 the sheriff's unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. The county attorney writes in May, offering payment agreements to eligible owners, and again in June. The clerk's site lays out the path to the annual sale.

Scott County Clerk delinquent tax calendar
DateStep
April 15Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk
May and JuneCounty Attorney mails notices and offers payment agreements
June 30Deadline to sign a payment agreement
July 1Advertising costs attach to remaining bills
August 21, 4:30 pmLast chance to pay and stay out of the sale
August 24, 8:30 amSale in the third-floor Fiscal Court Room

Those dates belong to the 2026 sale, which has passed, and the sequence repeats yearly with the dates shifted. The clerk takes cash, cashier's checks, money orders and cards, and a 2.75 percent vendor fee applies to cards. For payoff figures call the clerk at (502) 863-7875, extension 2260, or the County Attorney at (502) 863-7870 about agreements.

sections.h2: Where do I go in person for Scott County tax business?
sections.html:
• Sheriff (current-year bills): 240 Caleb Conley Way and 120 N Hamilton St, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Clerk (delinquent bills, deeds, motor vehicles): 101 E Main Street, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Attorney: 198 E Washington St, Georgetown.
  • Georgetown-Scott County Revenue Commission (occupational and business tax): (502) 603-5860.

The county Treasurer's page states that vehicle and property taxes are not collected in that office.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Scott County valuation or claim an exemption?
sections.html:
Kentucky makes a PVA conference the first step, and only after it can you petition the local appeals board, which wants comparable sales, repair bids or similar proof. An appeal does not suspend the bill, so pay on the value you claim while it runs.

The homestead exemption is open to owners past 65 and to those totally disabled, through the PVA. The state's deduction of $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 turns a $320,000 assessment into a $270,900 taxable base. The PVA can confirm the figure for the current year.

faqs.q: Which office takes Scott County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The Scott County Sheriff's Office, at (502) 863-7855, for current-year bills. Unpaid bills go to the County Clerk around April 15, and Georgetown's own city bill is paid through the city.

faqs.q: When was the last Scott County tax sale?
faqs.a: The 2026 sale was scheduled for August 24 at 8:30 am in the third-floor Fiscal Court Room, with payment due by 4:30 pm on August 21 to be left out of it. Later years follow the same pattern.

faqs.q: Is there a payment plan for delinquent Scott County tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. The County Attorney mails a May notice describing agreements for eligible owners, and June 30 is the cutoff to sign one. The office answers at (502) 863-7870.

faqs.q: Does a 65-year-old Scott County owner get the homestead exemption automatically?
faqs.a: No. File at the PVA, (502) 863-7885, with proof of age. The state deduction for 2025 and 2026 was $49,100.

faqs.q: Do Georgetown homeowners get a second property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, the city bills its own property tax. You can search and pay through the city's OpenGov portal or at the City Clerk's Office.
